name: Tartrazine (E102)
notes: Azo dye; alters microbiota composition, promotes intestinal inflammation via NF-κB

name: Allura Red AC (E129)
notes: Azo dye; promotes colitis via gut microbiota-serotonin signaling axis

name: Carrageenan (E407)
notes: Seaweed polysaccharide; disrupts mucus layer, activates TLR4/NF-κB, promotes bacterial translocation

name: Metformin
notes: First-line T2D biguanide; extensive gut microbiome remodelling (Forslund 2015, Wu 2017, Maier 2018)

name: Phenylacetylglutamine
notes: Gut microbial metabolite from phenylalanine; produced by Clostridiales; promotes platelet hyperreactivity and cardiovascular disease (Wang 2020 Cell)

name: NAFLD
notes: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease; Bacteroides/Prevotella ratio altered; gut-liver axis via portal vein LPS

name: Tight Junction Integrity
notes: Claudin-3/4, occludin, ZO-1; physical barrier of intestinal epithelium; butyrate upregulates via Akt/mTOR

name: LPS Translocation
notes: Lipopolysaccharide passage from gut lumen to systemic circulation via disrupted barrier; triggers TLR4-NF-κB cascade

name: PAGln Biosynthesis
notes: Phenylalanine → phenylacetic acid → PAGln via gut microbial enzymes; rate-limiting step is porA/fldA in Clostridiales

name: Hepatic Cholesterol Synthesis
notes: De novo cholesterol and fatty acid synthesis in liver; inhibited by propionate via AMPK activation (Chambers 2015 Gut)

name: NLRP3 Inflammasome
notes: NOD-like receptor pyrin domain-containing 3; innate immune sensor; activated by TMAO, LPS, DCA, succinate; produces IL-1β and IL-18; drives cardiac fibrosis and HF (Li 2019 Cardiovasc Res)

name: IL-18
notes: Interleukin-18; co-produced with IL-1β by NLRP3; promotes Th1 responses and endothelial inflammation

name: Endothelial Dysfunction
notes: Loss of NO bioavailability, increased VCAM-1/ICAM-1 expression; triggered by TMAO via PKC/NF-κB and oxidative stress; initiates atherosclerotic plaque formation

name: Succinate
notes: TCA cycle intermediate; also produced by gut bacteria; activates SUCNR1 on macrophages → M1 polarization → NLRP3 → inflammation

name: SUCNR1
notes: Succinate receptor 1 (GPR91); expressed on macrophages and dendritic cells; succinate ligation drives M1 polarization and NLRP3 activation

name: M1 Macrophage Polarization
notes: Pro-inflammatory macrophage phenotype; driven by succinate/SUCNR1, LPS/TLR4; produces TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, ROS; central driver of foam cell formation and atherogenesis

name: Cardiac Fibroblast Activation
notes: Transition of cardiac fibroblasts to myofibroblasts; driven by TMAO via TGF-β/SMAD2; leads to collagen I/III deposition and diastolic dysfunction

name: Indole-3-Propionic Acid
notes: Protective indole metabolite; produced from Trp by Clostridium sporogenes, Lactobacillus; activates PXR and AHR; anti-inflammatory, barrier-protective, reduces T2D risk (Roager 2018 Nat Commun)

name: Indole-3-Aldehyde
notes: AHR ligand produced by Lactobacillus reuteri from tryptophan; suppresses NF-κB and NLRP3; promotes Treg differentiation; protective in vascular inflammation

name: Tryptophanase
notes: Bacterial enzyme (tnaA gene) converting Trp → indole + pyruvate + ammonia; expressed by E. coli, Proteus, Bacteroides; first step in indoxyl sulfate production

name: Pregnane X Receptor
notes: Nuclear receptor activated by IPA; regulates xenobiotic metabolism; IPA-PXR axis promotes barrier gene expression (claudins, mucins) in enterocytes

name: Deoxycholic Acid
notes: Secondary bile acid produced from cholic acid by bacterial 7α-dehydroxylase (Ruminococcus, Clostridium); TGR5 agonist; cardioprotective at physiological concentrations; pro-inflammatory at high levels via NLRP3

name: Lithocholic Acid
notes: Secondary bile acid from CDCA by 7α-dehydroxylase; most potent TGR5 agonist (LCA>DCA>CDCA>CA); cardioprotective via TGR5-mediated platelet suppression; cytotoxic at high concentrations

name: 7α-Dehydroxylase
notes: Bacterial enzyme converting primary → secondary bile acids; encoded by bai operon (baiA-I genes); present in Ruminococcus gnavus, Clostridium scindens, some Blautia; rate-limiting step in secondary BA production

name: Chenodeoxycholic Acid
notes: Primary bile acid; FXR agonist (preferred); converted to LCA by gut bacterial 7α-dehydroxylase; regulates cholesterol homeostasis via FXR-SHP-LDLR axis

name: Ellagic Acid
notes: Polyphenol from pomegranates, berries, nuts; gut microbiota converts ellagitannins → ellagic acid → urolithins; interindividual variation in conversion determines cardiovascular benefit

name: PINK1/Parkin Mitophagy
notes: Selective autophagy of damaged mitochondria; PINK1 accumulates on depolarized mitochondria → Parkin recruitment → ubiquitination → autophagic clearance; urolithin A activates this pathway; declines with aging

name: Mitochondrial Dysfunction
notes: Accumulation of damaged mitochondria due to impaired mitophagy; produces excessive ROS; impairs cardiomyocyte energetics; contributes to HF progression and cardiac aging

name: Urolithin B
notes: Urolithin produced by gut bacteria from ellagic acid; reduces cardiac arrhythmia susceptibility post-AMI via anti-apoptotic and anti-fibrotic effects on cardiomyocytes (Huang 2022 Oxid Med Cell Longev)

name: Ruminococcaceae UCG-010
notes: MR-causal PROTECTIVE genus for both coronary and peripheral atherosclerosis (IVW OR=0.80, p=0.006; OR=0.65, p=0.013 respectively, MiBioGen+FinnGen); butyrate-producing Ruminococcaceae member

name: FUT2 (Secretor Gene)
notes: Fucosyltransferase 2; determines secretor status (ABO antigens in gut mucus); non-secretors (FUT2 loss-of-function) have 30-50% lower Bifidobacterium abundance; FUT2 is one of most replicated microbiome GWAS loci (MiBioGen, HUNT 2026 Nat Genet)

name: LCT (Lactase Gene)
notes: Lactase-phlorizin hydrolase; lactase persistence (LCT-13910C>T) determines dairy digestion; controls substrate availability for Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus; second most replicated microbiome GWAS locus

name: ABO Blood Group Gene
notes: ABO glycosyltransferase; blood group antigens expressed on gut epithelium act as binding sites for specific taxa; ABO locus associated with Ruminococcus, Faecalibacterium, Collinsella in MiBioGen GWAS

name: NOD2
notes: Nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain 2; innate immune receptor for muramyl dipeptide (bacterial cell wall); NOD2 variants (R702W, G908R, 1007fs) are IBD risk loci that specifically enrich Enterobacteriaceae; connects host immune genetics to microbial composition

name: Statins (HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitors)
notes: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (atorvastatin, simvastatin, rosuvastatin); widely prescribed in ACVD and MetaCardis cohorts; 24% of non-antibiotic drugs inhibit ≥1 gut bacterial strain in vitro (Maier 2018); statins increase Lactobacillaceae and Bifidobacterium, deplete some Clostridia

name: Aspirin (Acetylsalicylic Acid)
notes: COX inhibitor and antiplatelet agent; commonly co-prescribed in ACVD and T2D with CVD risk; shifts bile acid metabolism and alters Prevotella/Bacteroides ratio; Maier 2018 shows aspirin inhibits Fusobacterium nucleatum growth

name: ACE Inhibitors
notes: Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ramipril, enalapril); common in HF and HTN patients in MetaCardis; increase Akkermansia muciniphila abundance; suppress pathobiont expansion via RAAS-gut axis (Vieira-Silva 2020 Nat Med)

name: Proton Pump Inhibitors
notes: PPIs (omeprazole, pantoprazole); extremely common in cardiometabolic cohorts; dramatically alter gut microbiome by reducing gastric acid → small intestinal bacterial overgrowth; increase Enterococcus, Streptococcus; decrease Faecalibacterium, Ruminococcus (Vieira-Silva 2020 Nat Med)

name: CYP27A1
notes: Sterol 27-hydroxylase; alternative BA synthesis pathway (acidic pathway); converts cholesterol to 27-hydroxycholesterol → chenodeoxycholic acid; TMAO inhibits this pathway too

name: Reverse Cholesterol Transport
notes: Process by which cholesterol is transported from peripheral tissues back to liver for excretion as bile acids; impaired by TMAO via CYP7A1/CYP27A1 suppression; key anti-atherosclerotic mechanism; SR-B1 and ABCA1 are key transporters

name: LDL Accumulation
notes: Elevation of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in blood; occurs when RCT is impaired or LDL synthesis exceeds clearance; directly drives atherosclerotic plaque formation

name: Lactate
notes: Fermentation end-product of lactic acid bacteria and E. coli; cross-fed to propionate/butyrate producers; elevated in gut dysbiosis; can activate NLRP3 and promote inflammation at high concentrations

name: Urocanase (hutU)
notes: Bacterial urocanase; converts urocanate → imidazole propionate; encoded by hutU gene; expressed by Prevotella, Fusobacterium, Alistipes, Clostridiales; rate-limiting step in gut ImP production (Koh 2018 Cell)

name: p38γ MAPK
notes: p38 gamma mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK12); activated by ImP-mediated inhibition of IMPDH → depletion of GMP pools → stress kinase activation; phosphorylates IRS1-S307 → disrupts insulin receptor signaling → T2D (Koh 2018 Cell 175:947)

name: Histidine Catabolism Pathway
notes: Bacterial pathway: L-histidine → urocanate (histidase/hutH) → ImP (urocanase/hutU); host uses different pathway (formiminoglutamate); gut microbiota uniquely produces ImP via urocanase, which is absent in mammalian metabolism

name: Branched-Chain Amino Acids (BCAAs)
notes: Leucine, isoleucine, valine; dietary essential AAs; gut microbiota modulates circulating BCAA levels via catabolism (Bacteroidetes degrade BCAAs) and production (Firmicutes produce BCAAs from fermentation substrates); elevated plasma BCAAs are among the strongest metabolomics predictors of incident T2D and insulin resistance (Wang 2011 Nat Med, N=2,422)

name: BCAA Catabolism
notes: Degradation of leucine/isoleucine/valine via branched-chain aminotransferase (BCAT) and branched-chain keto-acid dehydrogenase (BCKDH) complex; impaired in insulin-resistant states (BCKDH kinase is upregulated); gut microbiota (especially Bacteroidetes) performs significant BCAA catabolism

name: Hydrogen Sulfide (H₂S)
notes: Gut microbiota-derived gasotransmitter; produced from sulfate reduction by Desulfovibrio and Bilophila via dissimilatory sulfite reductase (dsrAB); host also produces H₂S via CBS/CSE enzymes; cardioprotective at physiological concentrations (vasodilation via ATP-sensitive K⁺ channels, anti-platelet); cytotoxic at excess — inhibits cytochrome c oxidase (Complex IV) (Li 2011 PNAS, Mani 2014 Free Radic Biol Med)

name: Dissimilatory Sulfite Reductase (dsrAB)
notes: Key enzyme in anaerobic sulfate respiration; encoded by dsrAB gene pair; expressed in sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB): Desulfovibrio, Bilophila; reduces sulfate → sulfite → H₂S; requires taurine/bile acid-derived sulfate as electron acceptor in gut lumen

name: ATP-sensitive K⁺ Channel (KATP)
notes: K⁺ channel complex (Kir6.x/SURx) in vascular smooth muscle, cardiomyocytes, pancreatic β-cells; H₂S activates KATP via sulfhydration of Cys6 → membrane hyperpolarization → vasodilation and cardioprotection; pharmacological target of nicorandil (KATP opener, anti-anginal)

name: Vasodilation
notes: Relaxation of vascular smooth muscle → reduced peripheral resistance → decreased blood pressure; mediated by NO (eNOS→sGC→cGMP), H₂S (KATP), PGI2 (prostacyclin receptor); gut microbiota modulates all three pathways

name: Cardiac Glycoside Reductase (cgr operon)
notes: Two-component flavin-dependent reductase unique to Eggerthella lenta (cgr1/cgr2 genes); reduces and inactivates cardiac glycosides (digoxin, digitoxin); arginine-inducible; patients with Eggerthella-high microbiomes require higher digoxin doses for equivalent therapeutic effect (Haiser 2013 Science 341:295); paradigm case for microbiome pharmacokinetics

name: Digoxin
notes: Cardiac glycoside Na/K-ATPase inhibitor; used for rate control in AF and positive inotropy in HFrEF; narrow therapeutic window (0.5–2.0 ng/mL); Eggerthella cgr operon reduces bioavailability by inactivating digoxin in gut lumen before absorption; gut microbiome determines ~20% of digoxin PK variability (Haiser 2013, Javdan 2020)

name: Dopamine Dehydroxylase (ddc)
notes: Eggerthella lenta enzyme (ddc gene product) that converts dopamine → m-tyramine by removing the m-hydroxyl group; depletes gut lumen dopamine pool; relevant to enteric dopamine signaling and cardiometabolic gut-brain axis; Javdan 2020 Cell 181:1661 identified ddc as the cognate gene

name: m-Tyramine
notes: Eggerthella metabolite from dopamine dehydroxylation; trace amine; activates trace amine-associated receptor (TAAR1) on cardiac cells and platelets; potential pro-arrhythmic at elevated concentrations; poorly characterized in cardiometabolic context

name: Gut Microbial Drug Inactivation
notes: Process by which gut bacteria chemically modify drugs before/after absorption, reducing therapeutic bioavailability or converting to inactive/toxic forms; Eggerthella/cgr (digoxin), Prevotella/azo reductase (azo drugs), Clostridium/sulfatase (irinotecan reactivation); distinct from drug_promotes/drug_depletes — this is pharmacokinetic interference, not microbiome compositional shift

name: Mucin Degradation
notes: Enzymatic breakdown of mucin O-glycans by mucolytic bacteria (Akkermansia, Ruminococcus gnavus, Bacteroides); Akkermansia degrades mucin as its primary energy source → releases mucin precursors → signals goblet cells to replenish mucus layer → barrier renewal; functional mucin cycling is anti-inflammatory and maintains colonocyte energy supply

name: PorA (Phenylpyruvate Decarboxylase)
notes: Bacterial enzyme encoded by porA gene in Clostridiales (Clostridium sporogenes, Peptostreptococcus anaerobius); converts phenylpyruvate → phenylacetaldehyde → phenylacetate → conjugated with glutamine → PAGln; this is the gut-specific enzyme for PAGln synthesis, absent in humans; rate-limiting for PAGln production (Koeth 2019 Nat Med 25:1448)

name: α2A-Adrenergic Receptor (ADRA2A)
notes: G protein-coupled receptor (Gi/o); expressed on platelets, vascular smooth muscle, presynaptic neurons; PAGln activates ADRA2A on platelets → Gi → reduced cAMP → increased cytosolic Ca²⁺ → αIIbβ3 activation → platelet aggregation → thrombosis risk; ADRA2A on VSM → vasoconstriction → hypertension (Dempsey 2021 Cell 184:1053)

name: Urocanase (hutU, K01712)
notes: KEGG Orthology: urocanate hydratase; converts urocanate → imidazole propionate; encoded by hutU gene; expressed in Prevotella, Fusobacterium, Alistipes, Clostridiales; rate-limiting enzyme for gut ImP production; absent in human metabolism — gut-microbiome-specific reaction (Koh 2018 Cell 175:947)

name: Angiotensin II
notes: Vasoactive octapeptide; primary effector of RAAS; promotes vasoconstriction, aldosterone release, Na+ retention, renal renin secretion; gut microbiota modulates Ang II via ACE2 expression (SCFA → ACE2 upregulation); elevated in MetaCardis HF patients on ACEi therapy

name: Butyrate Kinase (buk/but pathway)
notes: Terminal enzyme in the butyrate kinase pathway (phosphotransbutyrylase + butyrate kinase); converts butyryl-phosphate → butyrate; expressed by Faecalibacterium, Roseburia, Eubacterium, Coprococcus, Anaerostipes; alternative but/buk pathway complements butyryl-CoA:acetate CoA-transferase

name: Beta-Blockers (β-Adrenergic Antagonists)
notes: β1/β2 adrenergic receptor blockers (metoprolol, carvedilol, bisoprolol); standard HF and HTN therapy; common in MetaCardis HF subgroup; alter gut motility via autonomic modulation → microbiome shifts (Vieira-Silva 2020 Nat Med); reduce gut transit time

name: Calcium Channel Blockers (CCBs)
notes: L-type Ca²⁺ channel blockers (amlodipine, nifedipine, diltiazem); used in HTN and angina; common in MetaCardis; alter gut smooth muscle contraction → microbiome niche effects; some show antimicrobial activity in Maier 2018 screen (Nature 555:623)

name: Propionate CoA-Transferase (pct/mmdA)
notes: Enzyme family producing propionate via two gut pathways: (1) acrylate pathway: lactate → acrylyl-CoA → propionyl-CoA → propionate; (2) succinate pathway: oxaloacetate → succinate → propionyl-CoA → propionate; expressed by Bacteroides, Prevotella, Roseburia, Ruminococcus; major propionate producer in human colon (Flint 2012)

name: Urease (ureC)
notes: Bacterial enzyme hydrolyzing urea → ammonia + CO₂; encoded by ureC gene; expressed by Klebsiella, E. coli, Enterococcus, Helicobacter; elevates colonic pH; elevated ammonia contributes to hepatic encephalopathy risk and gut dysbiosis maintenance

name: Lactate Dehydrogenase (ldh)
notes: Converts pyruvate → lactate (fermentative LDH); encoded by ldhA/ldhD genes; expressed by Lactobacillus, Streptococcus, Bifidobacterium, E. coli; lactate is a key cross-feeding metabolite linking fermenters to butyrate/propionate producers (Flint 2012)

name: IL18RAP (IL-18 Receptor Accessory Protein)
notes: IL-18 receptor accessory protein gene; IL18RAP locus is a significant microbiome GWAS hit in MiBioGen (Kurilshikov 2021 Nat Genet, n=18,340); IL-18 signaling modulates mucosal immune tolerance and IgA secretion, which regulate strict anaerobe colonization

name: DHODH (Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase)
notes: Rate-limiting enzyme in de novo pyrimidine synthesis; DHODH locus is a MiBioGen microbiome GWAS hit; DHODH activity in immune cells controls proliferation and IgA production → shapes mucosal immune pressure on gut microbiome composition

name: SLC39A8 (Manganese Transporter)
notes: Solute carrier family 39 member 8; encodes ZIP8 manganese transporter; SLC39A8 locus is a MiBioGen microbiome GWAS hit; Mn²⁺ is essential cofactor for many bacterial metalloenzymes; host Mn²⁺ transport shapes the luminal Mn²⁺ availability → selects for Mn-requiring bacteria

name: Urolithin A
notes: Ellagitannin metabolite; PINK1/Parkin mitophagy

name: Indole-3-propionic acid
notes: Tryptophan metabolite; gut barrier protector

name: Indole-3-acetic acid
notes: AHR ligand; anti-inflammatory

name: Indole-3-aldehyde
notes: AHR ligand; Treg-promoting

name: Tryptamine
notes: Serotonin precursor; gut motility
